subject: Kickoff: Performance tuning plan for ACME AI onboarding
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Ortega <jamie.ortega@acme-ai.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11 09:12 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Performance tuning plan for ACME AI onboarding

Hi Jamie / Priya —

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Following up with a concise plan for the performance and cost tuning work we'll run during your onboarding window (weeks 1–4). Goal: land a safe default config that meets your 95th%-latency target (~350ms p95 for text-generation endpoint under expected traffic) while minimizing per-token cost.

High-level phases (we'll run these in parallel where safe):
- Discovery (week 1): collect sample traffic, seq-len distribution, and target SLOs.
- Baseline & profiling (end of week 1): run baseline workload on hosted staging model to get latency / throughput curves.
- Iteration (weeks 2–3): evaluate batching policies, prefix/KV caching of common prompts, and 2–3 quantization profiles.
- Rollout (week 4): pick default profile + routing policy and push to canary then 100% with rollback hooks.

Immediate asks from your side:
1) Share a 24–48h sample of requests (anonymized headers/tokens) — Priya said she can provide this.
2) Confirm p95 latency and cost targets for initial launch.

I'll attach a short runbook and the candidate quant profiles we plan to test. Marissa will own the integration acceptance tests and Dev will run the profiling jobs. I'll coordinate the canary schedule with your SREs.

Proposed kickoff: Wednesday 2027-04-13 10:00 PT. Does that work?

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Date: 2027-04-11 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Performance tuning plan for ACME AI onboarding

Thanks Soojin — this looks great. Wednesday 4/13 10:00 PT works. We'll deliver a 48h anonymized sample by end of day Monday (4/12).

For targets: p95 ~350ms (we can go to 400ms if cost delta is large). Cost target: keep inferred per-token cost under $0.003 for the default profile. If you can sketch expected trade-offs for the quant profiles ahead of the call that would help.

Quick Q: do you recommend prefix caching for our customer-templates use case? We have a lot of repeated system prompts + product descriptions.

—Jamie
Director, Platform Engineering
ACME AI
jamie.ortega@acme-ai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Ortega <jamie.ortega@acme-ai.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12 08:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Performance tuning plan for ACME AI onboarding

Jamie — short answers inline below and a proposed test matrix we can run during the profile evaluation. We'll review on Wednesday.

> do you recommend prefix caching for our customer-templates use case?
Yes — prefix/KV caching is one of the highest win levers when you have a large percentage of repeated prefixes (system prompts + product descriptions). For your traffic mix, we typically see 25–45% token cost reduction and 10–25% p95 latency improvement once a cache warmed for common templates. We'll include warmup runs in week 1.

Proposed evaluation matrix (candidate axis):
- Quant profiles: FP16 baseline, 8-bit PTQ, 4-bit GPTQ candidate (3 profiles total).
- Batching policies: conservative (max batch size=8, max-delay=20ms), aggressive (size=64, delay=60ms), adaptive continuous batching based on observed qps.
- Caching modes: none, prefix-only, full KV (prefix + dynamic turn-level).
- Routing: single-stage (primary hosted model) vs fallback route (smaller quantized model) under queue-depth thresholds.

Deliverables by end of week 3:
- Latency/cost heatmap per-profile + recommended default
- Canary rollout plan (timing + rollback conditions)
- Simple monitoring dashboard (p95, error-rate, cost-per-1k-tokens) in Redwood Console

Attaching: batching_latency-metrics.xlsx (synthetic sim we use for sizing).

Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jamie Ortega <jamie.ortega@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme-ai.com>
Date: 2027-04-13 10:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Performance tuning plan for ACME AI onboarding

On Wed, Apr 13, 2027 at 10:00 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick sync notes and immediate action items:
> - Priya to upload 48h sample to the shared Drive link.
> - Dev to run baseline profiling on hosted staging model (FP16).
> - Marissa to prepare test harness for batching sims.
> - Soojin to schedule canary windows with ACME SRE.

Follow-ups from profiling run (started 4/13 afternoon):
- Baseline FP16 p95 (seq=160 median) = 420ms under target qps. CPU contribution minimal; most of the delta is kernel latency.
- Initial 8-bit PTQ reduced p95 to ~360ms but introduced a small hallucination-rate bump in a specific prompt family (tracking in JIRA RDW-3245).
- 4-bit GPTQ candidate brought p95 down to 320–340ms but increased token-generation variance; needs longer eval on quality set.

I'll gate the 4-bit profile behind quality Acceptance Criteria (QA) you define. For next steps I'll spin up two canaries: (A) FP16 baseline with prefix caching enabled and aggressive batching; (B) 4-bit candidate with conservative batching + canary routing (max 10% traffic).

Dev
Senior Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: run logs (linked in JIRA)

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme-ai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-14 15:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Performance tuning plan for ACME AI onboarding

Thanks team — the 48h sample is uploaded here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-onboarding-kickoff.

A couple of notes:
- Our typical sequence length distribution is bimodal (short chat 40–80 tokens, product-descriptions 140–220 tokens). We worry about tail behavior during product-descriptions spikes.
- Acceptance criteria for 4-bit: no measurable change in Rouge/EM on our eval set (within 1.5%), and no increase in user-reported quality issues for two consecutive days during the canary.

We'll review canary scheduling in tomorrow's 10am check-in.

—Priya
Head of SRE | ACME AI

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Performance tuning plan for ACME AI onboarding

Perfect, thanks everyone — quick next steps captured here: 
1) ACME to confirm exact canary windows (Priya) by EOD 4/16.
2) Dev to push canary configs: Canary A (FP16 + prefix cache + aggressive batching), Canary B (4-bit GPTQ + conservative batching + 10% traffic) — target start 4/19.
3) Marissa to publish the monitoring dashboard and set alerting thresholds in Redwood Console (p95 > 380ms, error-rate > 0.5%, quality-regression alert tied to eval sets).
4) Soojin will open the approval ticket for final rollout (deal link: https://app.redwood.com/deals/RDW-ACME-2027-07).

I've attached the onboarding runbook and the candidate quant profiles. We'll reconvene after 48h of canary data to pick the default.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth launch.

Soojin
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
